title: Positive-degree constant cohomology vanishes on closed subschemes of the spectrum of a normal domain with separably closed fraction field (Stacks 09ZC)
statement: Let $R$ be a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] whose field of fractions is separably closed [def-pc-separably-closed], and let $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $i:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] (a closed subscheme $Z\subseteq X$). Then for every finite abelian group $M$, with constant sheaf $\underline M$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] on $Z_{\Et}$, and every integer $q\ge1$, the etale cohomology group [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] $H^q(Z_{\Et},\underline M)$ is zero.

source.place: Lemma 09ZC (label lemma-gabber-for-absolutely-algebraically-closed), line 14445, and its proof; Stacks' hypothesis 'normal integral affine scheme with separably closed function field' is Spec of a normal domain with separably closed fraction field

proof.text: *Reduction to $Z=\operatorname{Spec}R'$ (Stacks: 'Write $X=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ and $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(R')$ so that we have a surjection of rings $R\to R'$').* Let $K$ be the fraction field of $R$. Since $i:Z\to X=\operatorname{Spec}R$ is a closed immersion, by the affine form of [def-weil-closed-immersion] (Stacks 01QO, applied to the affine open $U=X$) there are an ideal $I\subseteq R$ and an isomorphism of schemes $\varphi:Z\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Spec}R'$ over $X$, where $R'=R/I$ and $\operatorname{Spec}R'\to X$ is induced by the quotient map $R\to R'$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Transport of structure along $\varphi$: the functor $\Phi:Z_{\Et}\to(\operatorname{Spec}R')_{\Et}$, $(U\xrightarrow{u}Z)\mapsto(U\xrightarrow{\varphi u}\operatorname{Spec}R')$, identity on morphisms, is an isomorphism of categories (inverse via $\varphi^{-1}$) [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]; it sends a family $\{U_k\to U\}$ to the same family, so it preserves and reflects coverings, and it sends the final object $Z$ to the final object $\operatorname{Spec}R'$. Hence $G\mapsto G\circ\Phi^{-1}$ is an isomorphism between the categories of abelian sheaves, which preserves injective objects, exactness, K-injective resolutions and global sections, and sends the constant presheaf with value $M$ to the constant presheaf, hence (sheafification being determined by its universal property) $\underline M_Z$ to $\underline M_{\operatorname{Spec}R'}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Therefore $H^q(Z_{\Et},\underline M)\cong H^q((\operatorname{Spec}R')_{\Et},\underline M)$ for all $q$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], and it suffices to show $H^q((\operatorname{Spec}R')_{\Et},\underline M)=0$ for $q\ge1$. The same transport applies to any isomorphism of schemes; it is used again in step 4.

source.place: Lemma 09ZC (label lemma-gabber-for-absolutely-algebraically-closed), line 14445, proof, first sentence; the transport along the isomorphism Z = Spec(R') is left implicit by Stacks

proof.text: *The local rings of $R$ are strictly henselian (Stacks: 'by Lemma 09Z9').* $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$ is an integral scheme whose function field is (isomorphic as an $R$-algebra to) $K$, and $\mathcal O_{X,\mathfrak p}\cong R_{\mathfrak p}$ for every prime $\mathfrak p$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field]. Each $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a localization of the normal domain $R$ at $S=R\setminus\mathfrak p\not\ni0$, hence a normal domain [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain]; so all local rings of $X$ are normal domains, i.e. $X$ is a normal integral scheme [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], and its function field $K$ is separably closed by hypothesis [def-pc-separably-closed]. By part (2) of [sbc-lem-etale-over-normal] (Stacks 09Z9; sorry-free Lean in slopmaster2: AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.exists_opens_isOpenImmersion_and_henselianLocalRing_stalk, whose hypotheses are IsIntegral S, every stalk integrally closed, IsSepClosed S.functionField) every local ring $\mathcal O_{X,\mathfrak p}\cong R_{\mathfrak p}$ is strictly henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology].

proof.text: *The local rings of $R'$ are strictly henselian (Stacks: '... and Algebra, Lemma 05WS').* Let $\mathfrak p'$ be a prime of $R'=R/I$ and $\mathfrak p\supseteq I$ its preimage in $R$, so $\mathfrak p'=\mathfrak p/I$. Localization is exact, so localizing $0\to I\to R\to R'\to0$ at $R\setminus\mathfrak p$ (whose image in $R'$ is $R'\setminus\mathfrak p'$) gives $R'_{\mathfrak p'}\cong R_{\mathfrak p}/IR_{\mathfrak p}$, and $IR_{\mathfrak p}\subseteq\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$, the maximal ideal, since $I\subseteq\mathfrak p$. By step 2, $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is strictly henselian, so $R'_{\mathfrak p'}$ is strictly henselian by [lem-weil-pbc-strictly-henselian-quotient] [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology].

Since $R_f$ is a normal domain with separably closed fraction field we see that $H^1_{\Et}(D(f'),\underline M)=0$ by Lemma 09ZB').* Let $h\in R'$ and let $j_h:D(h)	o\operatorname{Spec}R'$ be the principal open subscheme. Claim: $H^1(D(h)_{\Et},j_h^{-1}\underline M)=0$. First, $j_h^{-1}\underline M\cong\underline M_{D(h)}$ [lemma-constructible-pullback-constant] [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Choose $f\in R$ mapping to $h$. If $f=0$ then $h=0$ and $D(h)=\emptyset$: the small etale site of the empty scheme has the single object $\emptyset$, covered by the empty family, so every abelian sheaf on it is $0$ and all its cohomology groups vanish. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-quotient-commute] (with $B=R$, $J=I$, $b=f$, $ ar b=h$) $R'_h\cong R_f/IR_f$, compatibly with the maps from $R_f$, so $R_f	o R'_h$ is surjective with kernel $IR_f$; so the morphism $\operatorname{Spec}R'_h	o\operatorname{Spec}R_f$ is a closed immersion [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-closed-immersion]. By [lem-weil-pbc-gabber-h1-absolutely-algebraically-closed] (Stacks 09ZB) applied to $R_f$ and this closed immersion, $H^1((\operatorname{Spec}R'_h)_{\Et},\underline M)=0$. proof.text: *Conclusion by Gabber's criterion (Stacks: 'Thus we may apply Lemma 0GY0 to $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(R')$ to conclude').* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-gabber-criterion] (Stacks 0GY0) to the ring $R'$ and the abelian sheaf $\mathcal F=\underline M$ on $(\operatorname{Spec}R')_{\Et}$: all local rings of $R'$ are strictly henselian by step 3, and for all $f,g\in R'$ the map $H^1(D(f+g)_{\Et},\mathcal F|_{D(f+g)})\to H^1(D(f(f+g))_{\Et},\mathcal F|_{D(f(f+g))})\oplus H^1(D(g(f+g))_{\Et},\mathcal F|_{D(g(f+g))})$ has zero kernel because its source is $0$ by step 4 (with $h=f+g$). Hence $H^q((\operatorname{Spec}R')_{\Et},\underline M)=0$ for all $q\ge1$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], and by step 1 $H^q(Z_{\Et},\underline M)=0$ for all $q\ge1$.
